For my dog, I initially entrusted him to Dr. Longobardi, who over time performed several vaccinations and surgeries, including teeth cleanings, specialist visits, and hair growth treatments.
At a certain point, for personal reasons, I chose not to give him his final booster shot and not to proceed with preventative kneecap surgery.
Unfortunately, my dog ​​passed away.
And for this very reason, I feel an even stronger need to share an episode that has remained deeply in my memory.
My dog ​​was a Miniature German Spitz, a breed we knew was predisposed to certain respiratory problems.
On one occasion, he had a respiratory problem, and naturally, I was immediately alarmed.
I wrote to the vet, but received no response.
Since he was my only point of contact at the time, I panicked and picked up the dog and went straight to the office.
Once I arrived, I was told that he was busy with the technicians in the office and that he couldn't even stop for a moment to see the dog.
I felt, essentially, like the door was slammed in my face precisely when I was most worried and scared.
I fully understand that a veterinarian can be busy and that it's not always possible to see an animal without an appointment.
What I missed, however, was even a simple gesture of humanity, a moment to listen to me, reassure me, or tell me what to do in a situation that, for me, was an emergency.
I hold the veterinarian in no way responsible for my dog's death.
What I can say is that in that moment I felt completely alone and without a point of reference.
And today, now that my dog ​​is no longer with us, that memory hurts even more.
For me, professionalism is fundamental, but when working with animals, I believe that empathy, availability, and the ability to understand the fear and desperation of those facing a potential problem are also an important part of one's job.
At that moment, unfortunately, I didn't perceive them.

Miraculous rescue! Thanks to Dr. Annunziata for her prompt surgery on my dog ​​(a ruptured spleen). A huge thank you also to Dr. Lombardo and the anesthesiologist, so talented and sweet, for the care they gave my little Kelly. If my little girl is still here today, it's thanks to them.
Do we realize how much a single second can make a difference in this life? And how meeting the right people can change the course of things! Best regards.
Very kind, attentive and well-trained veterinarians
I highly recommend this veterinary clinic. Professionalism, humanity, and honesty. These are the key words. Far from being a given these days.
Dr. Annunziata is a serious professional and an excellent surgeon, who operated on one of my four puppies for laxity of the hind leg knee.

Terrible experience. This morning I took my cat, who suffers from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, to the doctor for an abdominal ultrasound of his bladder because I had been noticing some blood in his urine for days. The doctor didn't recommend having him undergo a cardiology exam first to determine if he could be sedated. It wasn't his first visit; the doctor knew the cat well and knew he gets agitated during visits, so it was his moral duty to remind me how to sedate him and perform the exam safely. Conclusion: after accusing and blaming me for not having had him undergo a cardiology exam first, I left without him examining the cat. During the exam, he demanded that we, the owner, restrain the cat, but to no avail. A venal person to the max, as, after several years of caring for the cat, he even asks us for prescriptions. Extremely expensive and careless. This morning we wasted time, and I'm also pregnant with a small child who was forced to wake up early for her appointment. I hope the doctor understands how unprofessional he was. He's definitely lost clients, including me.
